newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of PMI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of PMI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Monday.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. March Chicago Purchasing Managers index (PMI), which is forecast to rise to 57.0 percent compared with 56.2 percent reported in February.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. Everyone is waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the Chicago PMI for March," a local dealer said.
"But it will probably be a non-event as most people are waiting for this Friday's issue of (the) employment report for March," he said.

In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday was indicated at 7-1/2 7-3/8 percent, due mainly to the turn of the new Japanese fiscal year, which begins on Tuesday. Week-fixed was unchanged from last Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from last Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, nine-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent.
